newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russia security chief flies to Chechnya - agency.
newsitem.headline: New Russia security chief flies to Chechnya - agency.

text.p: New Russian security chief Ivan Rybkin left Moscow on Sunday to pay his first visit to breakaway Chechnya, during which he may meet a leading rebel, Interfax news agency said.
Rybkin, who replaced the outspoken Alexander Lebed earlier this month, was heading for the neighbouring republic of Ingushetia from where he would continue to the Chechen capital Grozny by car.

Interfax, quoting a source in the administration of President Boris Yeltsin, said Rybkin would hold talks with commanders of Russian troops in the region and might also meet rebel chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov during the one-day trip.
In late August Lebed brokered a peace deal between Moscow and the Chechen separatists but the rebels say they are worried that his sacking could undermine the peace process.

Rybkin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin have been at pains to reassure the separatists that Moscow does not want a return to violence. Tens of thousands of people were killed in the 21 months of war before the August 31 peace deal.

But conservative Kremlin officals and members of parliament oppose the peace deal, which called for the withdrawal of all Russian troops and said discussions on Chechnya's future status should be put on hold for five years.
Separatist leaders said on Saturday they opposed Moscow's plans to keep two brigades in Chechnya permanently.
The rebels, who saw the peace deal as a face-saving way for Moscow to let Chechnya go, insist all Russian troops should leave. Moscow has ruled out granting independence to Chechnya.
